title: The Blue Key
verdict: Celine Ames was responsible for the disappearance of a scholarship decision envelope.
intent: Celine Ames wanted to delay a decision that would reveal favoritism in the award process.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the mailroom supervisor controlled the scanner reboot and the scholarship slot.
Remove a scholarship decision envelope from its checked location.
Hide the item in a hollow sorting-bin label holder.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: a scholarship decision envelope disappeared from a university mailroom during scholarship notification week.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.
The disappearance occurred within a narrow time window because the package scanner rebooted during the afternoon sort.
The physical trace was paper dust below the scholarship mail slot.
The relevant tool or mechanism was a letter opener with glue on its tip.
The item could be concealed in a hollow sorting-bin label holder.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the mailroom supervisor knew the sorting-bin label holder slid open.
The access pattern mattered because the mailroom supervisor controlled the scanner reboot and the scholarship slot.
distractor_cues: an applicant repeatedly asking about the envelope
a driver rushing through the sorting area
A visible conflict is suspicious but insufficient without timing and mechanism.
A bulky object or nervous behavior is insufficient unless it explains the hidden container.
